t: IoT Device Registry - public implementations survey
title: IoT Device Registry - public implementations survey
definition: Records connected devices, identifiers, and capabilities.
description:
IoT Device Registry is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Records connected devices, identifiers, and capabilities. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns IoT Device Registry. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves IoT Device Registry. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the IoT Device Registry capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: CoAP - related IoT Device Registry technology
title: CoAP - related IoT Device Registry technology
definition: Constrained REST for tiny devices.
description:
CoAP is not itself an IoT Device Registry, but it belongs in this survey because real IoT Device Registry work leans on it. Constrained REST for tiny devices.

In an IoT Device Registry build it shows up when the team already lives in its ecosystem. The design favors boring reliability over cleverness: well-trodden paths, clear errors, and behavior you can reason about without reading the source. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best IoT Device Registry practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, CoAP is a strong default choice as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.

t: IoT Device Registry definition of done - practitioner discipline
title: IoT Device Registry definition of done - practitioner discipline

description:
definition of done is the IoT Device Registry discipline: Records connected devices, identifiers, and capabilities. It turns IoT Device Registry from an event into a repeatable capability.

In practice this means: log every decision with its reason, so the next builder inherits understanding; verify outputs against the original request, not against your hopes; keep a failure log: what broke, why, and what now prevents it Teams that follow the discipline get predictable builds; teams that skip it get interesting stories. The Signature line prefers predictable builds, and this record's demo makes the discipline concrete and runnable.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of IoT Device Regist
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of IoT Device Regist
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of IoT Device Registry from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of IoT Device Registry from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the IoT Device Registry needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: you can list them from memory without looking at the brief
